extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners / patent prosecutors / patent attorneys
extracted.subtask_description: Using examiner-level statistics (grant/allowance rates and timelines) to estimate examiner difficulty and the probability/timing of obtaining a granted patent. Compares conventional backward-looking allowance metrics to a forward-looking three-year grant probability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Backward grant rate (allowance rate)
rubrics_metrics.description: The most commonly used statistic is a grant rate or allowance rate that provides insight into the difficulty of an examiner. This statistic looks backward to tell you what percentage of applications that have already been disposed, were granted (granted/(granted + abandoned)). I’ll call this the backward grant rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commonly used by practitioners to gauge examiner difficulty. Computation: granted ÷ (granted + abandoned). Limitation: it's backward-looking (measures only already-disposed applications) and does not indicate timing for when a pending application might be granted; may be less accurate for predicting future outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-year grant rate
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'three-year grant rate' that shows the probability of obtaining a granted patent within three years of the first office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed as a forward-looking statistic to indicate both difficulty and expected timing: it tells you how difficult an examiner is and when you can expect to be granted a patent. The post claims this is a more accurate measure of examiner difficulty than the conventional backward grant rate for predicting future outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant rate timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: A timeline representation of grant rates (example: 'grant rate timeline across the entire USPTO').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to visualize how grant rates change over time and to compare trends across examiners or the whole USPTO. Serves as an illustrative tool alongside summary metrics (backward or three-year grant rates) to understand temporal patterns in allowance behavior.
